newsitem.title: UK: Bass drops after negative press report.
newsitem.headline: Bass drops after negative press report.

text.p: Shares in Bass Plc dropped early on Thursday as a press report said its brewing chief was to quit and that its planned 205 million stg takeover of rival brewer Carlsberg-Tetley would be blocked.
The stock was quoted down 3p at 756-1/2 by 0725 GMT, though no volume was recorded.

A report in the Guardian newspaper said Bass Brewers chief executive Iain Napier was set to quit to join Rank Group Plc, adding that the UK government was expected to block Bass's purchase of Allied-Domecq's 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.
The acquisition would have made Bass Britain's biggest brewer.
Analysts said uncertainty over the takeover of Carlsberg-Tetley had already weighed on Bass shares for some months. "The general sentiment is that they won't get it", an analyst said.
Most brokers would than revise their earnings estimates as Bass could not achieve the expected cost savings, he said.
Another analyst said he expected the Labour government not to veto the acquisition outright but to impose tough conditions which would effectively block the deal.
"Labour doesn't want to have such a big brewery group", he said.
Meanwhile, industry sources dismissed the report of Napier's departure to Rank, whose shares were up 7p at 378.
By 0813 GMT, Bass shares were down 5-1/2p at 754.
